The Software Testing and QA internship in short

The SkillMe Software Testing and QA internship is a 4-week, fully remote programme open to students worldwide. Over four weekly milestones you build QuestGuard: Test Plan, Bugs and Automation Suite for a Real App, post each milestone publicly on LinkedIn, and have it reviewed against clear acceptance criteria. Reviewers include engineers who work at Walmart, Google and LinkedIn. Top performers earn a stipend of up to $100 a month, and interns who get 3 of 4 milestones approved earn a QR-verified certificate and a Letter of Recommendation.

What you build

One real project, built over four weeks

Every intern on this track builds the same project, milestone by milestone.

QuestGuard: Test Plan, Bugs and Automation Suite for a Real App

Build a full QA workflow around a real public web app: a test plan, real bug reports, an automated UI test suite, an API test suite, and a coverage report that proves it all holds together.

  1. W1Test Planning and Manual Test Execution

Week by week

What each week of the Software Testing and QA internship covers

The four milestones of QuestGuard: Test Plan, Bugs and Automation Suite for a Real App.

  1. Week 1 of 4

    Test Planning and Manual Test Execution

    Beginner2-3 hours

    Pick a real public web app (a to-do list app, a demo e-commerce site, or similar), write a proper test plan for its core flow, and manually execute it to find real bugs. Good automation later depends on a clear, well-scoped test plan now.

    What you learn

    • Writing a test plan: scope, test cases, priorities, and pass/fail criteria
    • Designing test cases covering happy path, edge cases and negative cases
    • Manual test execution and recording results objectively
    • Distinguishing a bug from expected behavior

    What you submit

    • A written test plan with scope, environment and out-of-scope items
    • At least 15 test cases covering happy path, edge cases and negative cases
    • A test execution record with actual results and pass/fail status per case
    • A results summary with pass/fail counts and a risk assessment
  2. Week 2 of 4

    Bug Reports and Regression Tracking

    Beginner+2-3 hours

    Turn last week's found issues into proper bug reports that a real engineering team could act on without back-and-forth, and build a lightweight regression checklist to re-test after fixes. Writing a bug report that gets fixed on the first read is its own skill.

    What you learn

    • Writing a bug report with clear repro steps, expected vs actual, and severity
    • Assigning severity and priority independently and justifying each
    • Capturing evidence (screenshots, console logs, network requests)
    • Building a lightweight regression checklist for re-testing after a fix

    What you submit

    • At least 5 fully written bug reports with severity and priority justified separately
    • Evidence (screenshot or console/network capture) attached to each bug report
    • A bug tracker (spreadsheet, GitHub Issues, or board) with status tracking
    • A regression checklist of 8-10 checks covering the core flow and reported bugs
  3. Week 3 of 4

    Automated UI Test Suite

    Intermediate2-3 hours

    Automate the core flow from your test plan using Playwright (or Selenium), turning your manual test cases into a repeatable suite that catches regressions automatically. This is where QA work becomes engineering.

    What you learn

    • Setting up Playwright (or Selenium) with Python for browser automation
    • Writing reliable locators and avoiding flaky waits/sleeps
    • Structuring automated tests with setup/teardown and reusable helper functions
    • Generating a readable test report from an automated run

    What you submit

    • A Playwright (or Selenium) test suite automating 5-8 test cases from Week 1
    • A Page Object helper module used by the tests
    • Reliable locators with no fixed time.sleep() waits
    • An HTML (or equivalent) test report generated from a run
  4. Week 4 of 4

    API Test Suite, Coverage Report and CI

    Intermediate+2-3 hours

    Add an API-level automated test suite (faster and more precise than UI tests for many checks), wire both suites into CI, and produce a coverage report tying test cases back to your original test plan. This is the deliverable that shows a complete, professional QA process.

    What you learn

    • Writing automated API tests with requests or Postman/Newman
    • Testing status codes, response schemas and error responses at the API layer
    • Mapping test cases to a traceability/coverage report against the original test plan
    • Running both UI and API suites automatically in CI

    What you submit

    • An automated API test suite covering 4-6 endpoints with status, schema and response-time checks
    • A traceability/coverage report mapping every original test case to its automation status
    • A GitHub Actions CI workflow running both UI and API suites on every push
    • A final QA summary report with coverage percentage, bug status and known gaps

Software Testing and QA internship: questions and answers

What will I build in the Software Testing and QA internship?

You build QuestGuard: Test Plan, Bugs and Automation Suite for a Real App. Build a full QA workflow around a real public web app: a test plan, real bug reports, an automated UI test suite, an API test suite, and a coverage report that proves it all holds together. It is one project built up over four weekly milestones, so each week adds to the last.

Is the Software Testing and QA internship paid? Is there a stipend?

Top performers earn a stipend of up to $100 a month. The stipend is performance-based and is not paid to every intern: it goes to the interns whose reviewed work stands out in their cohort.

Who reviews my work?

Every weekly submission is reviewed against that week's acceptance criteria by the SkillMe team, which includes engineers who work at Walmart, Google and LinkedIn. Work that misses the bar comes back with notes on what to fix.

Do I need experience to apply for the Software Testing and QA internship?

You need the basics of Test Automation, Selenium, Bug Reports, not prior internship experience. Week 1 starts at Beginner level and week 4 reaches Intermediate+. A short screening quiz (8 questions, about 5 minutes) checks you are ready to start.

How long is the internship and how much time does it take?

It runs for 4 weeks with one milestone a week. Each milestone is planned for about 2-3 hours, and it is fully remote, so you work at your own pace around college or a job.

Who can apply? Is it open outside India?

Anyone can apply, from any country, college or year, and we encourage you to. Selection is competitive: every application is read by a person, and shortlisted applicants hear back within 48 hours.

What do I get when I finish?

An offer letter when you are selected, a public portfolio page with every approved milestone, and a QR-verified certificate and Letter of Recommendation once 3 of your 4 milestones are approved. Top performers also earn the stipend and are referred to hiring partners.
